summary: A01 CONFIRMED: the frame-directory guard checks only scene, fps and count, and encode trusts whatever 0000..N-1 PNGs sit in the directory, so a partial, low-resolution or low-spp render can become the canonical build/out video.
failure_scenario: After a full canonical Dolly render, run `render_motion.py --frames 10 --spp 1` or `--res 320x180` with the default --out. check_frame_directory allows it because canonical_sequence() ignores res, spp and frames. Then `--encode --no-render` (or an interrupted build/STOP_GPU re-render followed by --no-render) encodes the mixed set to build/out/dolly.mp4, which build_media copies to public media. A fully re-rendered `--res 320x180 --encode` publishes a low-resolution canonical video the same way.
evidence: Source trace of check_frame_directory (55-60), canonical_sequence (49-52), parse_args (--frames subset allowed without --encode) and encode (143-170: only file existence per index). Encode checks no resolution or provenance across frames, apart from the NVENC dimension-match check inside video_io. No GPU run.

summary: A03 CONFIRMED: no prim named RollingRoadFrame is ever authored (build_env authors RollingRoadBelt, Slot, Drums, Plates), so by_name returns None and the frame width falls back to the belt width, weakening the belt/wheel check and misreporting its figures.
failure_scenario: fr_hw becomes 48.5 (belt half width) instead of about 60 (plates reach hx+frame_w = 50+10). The committed fit-check.md line 181 says 'with its frame it is 97.0 wide ... 28.8 to spare each side'; the true spare to the frame is about 17.3 (77.3-60). A car whose inner tyre face lies at |X| between 48.5 and 60 would PASS 'Belt runs between the wheels' although the frame plates would hit the tyres.
evidence: grep shows RollingRoadFrame appears only in fit_check.py:572; build_env.py:508-522 and CFG belt (hw 50, frame_w 10) give the plate extent. Arithmetic from the values committed in models/wind_tunnel/docs/fit-check.md. Report not regenerated (needs pxr).

summary: A20 CONFIRMED: despite the 'explicit first-party paths only' docstring, the source archive globs docs/*.md and tools/*.py, so any untracked file in those directories is shipped with a valid SHA256SUMS entry.
failure_scenario: A scratch probe (CLAUDE.md expects throwaway probes next to tools/) or private note saved as tools/probe_x.py or docs/notes.md is zipped into stagewright-source.zip. source_bytes() only rejects build/external/.venv/.git and symlinks, not untracked files.
evidence: Source read of lines 1, 117-120 and source_bytes (65-73). Not executed; no archive built.

summary: A04 CONFIRMED: the jet-window clearance uses only mesh vertices, and u_profile has vertices only at the feet and corner arcs, so the flat roof is not measured; the reported clearance is too large and a low roof can pass.
failure_scenario: Nozzle exit (hw 325, h 400, r 40): vertex minimum 181.0 (side foot) as printed in fit-check.md:151, while the roof is only 400-248 = 152 above the domain top. With exit_h = 200 (roof inside the domain's Z range) the vertex test still gives min 141 and 0 vertices inside, so the check passes although the roof cuts through the domain. The accompanying note only discusses arc sagitta.
evidence: CPU stand-in of the profile vertex set (mesh_compute.profile count 2*(arc+1)+2, meshlib.u_profile) and rect_dist arithmetic. The current environment is unaffected for pass/fail; only the reported figure and the guard strength are wrong.

summary: A22 CONFIRMED: the off-centre turntable recommendation hard-codes a 450 cm belt half length and prints Y centre+450, but CFG belt half_len is 380.
failure_scenario: Edit CFG turntable cy so the centred check fails: the generated text says the belt reaches about Y y+450 (the committed fit-check.md shows belt Y -287..473 for cy 93, i.e. cy+380), overstating the overshoot past the domain inlet at Y 430 by 70 cm and possibly flagging a belt that fits.
evidence: build_env.py:98 half_len 380 and its comment; fit-check.md:181 belt Y range; fit_check.py:1058-1059.

summary: A19 CONFIRMED: the optional GIF is built from the %04d.png pattern, while the MP4 uses the explicit 0..count-1 list.
failure_scenario: Re-render --count 100 into a custom --out that still holds 0100..0215 from an earlier longer run, then `--encode --gif`: the MP4 has 100 frames and the GIF reads every consecutive file, including the stale ones. Only the optional ffmpeg path is affected.
evidence: Source read (162-181). ffmpeg image2 reads consecutive numbers from 0 until the first gap (documented behaviour, not run here).

summary: A07 CONFIRMED: reported travel and rotation are measured against the first recorded sample, which is taken after physics step 1, so motion during step 1 is excluded.
failure_scenario: simulate.py records seconds = 1/fps..steps/fps and no initial pose (115-116). A body that jumps in step 1 (depenetration, joint correction, strong initial velocity) and then stays still reports 0 in feedback.json; a moving body under-reports by one step. Overlap or snap corrections are exactly what a constructor would want surfaced.
evidence: Source trace simulate.py:89-116 and engine.measure (17-20). No physics run; solver behaviour at step 1 is native and not established.

summary: A12 CONFIRMED (arithmetic): max_rotation_degrees uses 2*arccos(|dot|) on normalized quaternions, so a body that never rotated can report about 0.04 to 0.08 degrees.
failure_scenario: With identical float32 rows (stationary body) about 30% of random quaternions give a unit dot of 0.99999994 or less, so arccos yields 0.0396 to 0.0791 degrees instead of 0. In float64 the same inputs give at most 3.4e-6 degrees.
evidence: numpy probe on 2000 random float32 quaternions, replicating measure() lines 19-21. ovphysx tensor dtype was not executed; float32 is assumed. Translation is unaffected (exact subtraction of identical rows).

summary: A02 CONFIRMED (inference): recorded poses are matrix4d time samples, which USD interpolates element-wise, so evaluation between samples is a non-rigid transform for large per-sample rotations.
failure_scenario: A body turning 30 degrees per sample (10 rev/s at the default 120 Hz) is evaluated at a fractional time by the observer playhead, whose per-tick advance is wall-clock now-tick and is not sample-aligned. At the midpoint the linear blend (I+R)/2 scales the plane by cos(15)=0.966 (determinant 0.933); 60 degrees gives 0.866. At 5 degrees the error is 0.1% and negligible. The snapshot path is exact when --fps divides the recording rate.
evidence: numpy probe of the blend. USD matrix4d linear interpolation is assumed from USD semantics (pxr is not installed here), and ovrtx evaluation was not run.

summary: A06 CONFIRMED (narrowed): Command and Publication errors are cleared only when a candidate revision is accepted or the render-pending message resolves, not on later successful polls or commands.
failure_scenario: A rejected seek (for example NaN) sets 'Command not accepted' (189), and a pinned viewer (select_revision, follow False) that hits the list-then-read race gets 'Publication not available'; both stay in state['error'] and app.js showError until the next revision switch, even though later commands and polls succeed. The stated follow-mode trigger self-heals, since the next poll sees revision N, switches, and sets error=None at line 306.
evidence: Source trace of every state['error'] write (95,104,152,189,210,258,306,312,314) and app.js showError.

summary: A21 CONFIRMED (narrow): the override layer name depends only on scene stem and ghost flag and is always written to build/stills, even when render_motion uses a custom --out.
failure_scenario: Two concurrent runs of the same scene with clean visibility (Dolly and Orbit360 on present, or stills Hero plus a motion run) write build/stills/_override_present_clean.usda. render_motion writes the layer, then waits for open_renderer before loading it, so the second writer can replace it. The first run then loads the other product's resolution and spp overrides, or none for its own product. Sequential runs are unaffected.
evidence: Source trace render.py:36-80 and render_motion.py:94-128. Race not executed; concurrent runs are a user choice.

summary: A18 CONFIRMED (render.py part only): os.path.relpath(scene, out_dir) raises on Windows when the scene and build/stills are on different drives.
failure_scenario: `render.py --scene D:/replay/view.usda` or render_motion.py --scene on another drive with the repo on C: raises ValueError before rendering. The physics_usd.py:89 half is rejected: relpath(source, recording) compares input.usdz and recording/ inside the same destination directory, so it stays on one drive. The failure is loud and writes nothing.
evidence: ntpath.relpath('D:/replay/view.usda','C:/repo/build/stills') raises ValueError 'path is on mount D:, start on mount C:' in a Linux CPU probe.

summary: A09 CONFIRMED: the NaN guard runs after ux.saveStage, so a NaN-bearing file stays at the published path although CLAUDE.md says the build scripts refuse to save one. The same ordering is in build_present.py:389-391.
failure_scenario: If an intermittent NaN matrix is authored, test_section.usda is written and then RuntimeError is raised; the bad asset remains for later tools until the build is rerun. The failure is loud, so impact is limited to a stale bad file in the working tree.
evidence: Source read of build_env.py:776-778 and build_present.py:389-391.

summary: A15 CONFIRMED (narrow): the staleness check hashes only scenes/present.usda, a thin root that references assets/test_section.usda, so environment or texture edits leave the record looking current.
failure_scenario: Edit assets/test_section.usda or a texture, keep present.usda and the public orbit360.mp4 unchanged: record scene_sha256 still matches and both archives ship the old video with the new source. A re-render changes the video hash and forces check_loop again, so the gap is only an un-rerendered video. The record certifies loop seam properties of that exact video, which stay true, so impact is limited. A17 shares the underlying media-freshness root.

summary: A16 CONFIRMED: README.md is packaged in both archives without the images and docs it links.
failure_scenario: README.md references docs/assets/courtyard-story.gif, courtyard-closed.png, courtyard-open.png and docs/live-viewer.md. The review archive carries only the svg, media and three model docs; the source archive adds docs/*.md but not the courtyard images. Unzipped README shows broken images; index.html does not use them.
evidence: README.md lines 15, 19, 41 against build_share.py review/sources lists.

summary: A08 CONFIRMED: check_loop decodes through NVDEC and nvImageCodec (via image_io.read_rgb) without constructing a GpuPacer, so it gets no priority, affinity or stop handling. build_media.py has the same root (JPEG encode and decode through image_io with no pacer).
failure_scenario: Running check_loop.py on the desktop starts GPU decode at normal priority and ignores build/STOP_GPU, contrary to the CLAUDE.md rule for shared GPU workers. Work is eight frames plus one video decode, so impact is small.
evidence: Source read: no gpu_work import in check_loop.py or build_media.py, while render_motion, rtx and video_io all call GpuPacer(). ImageCodec itself does not.

summary: A05 UNVERIFIED: video_pixels applies limited-range BT.601 and the code authors no colour tags. CPU arithmetic shows decoding that as BT.709 gives (255,0,0)->(255,25,0) after clipping and (60,180,90)->(51,163,88), matching the claim. Whether NVENC or the muxer writes VUI/colr metadata, and which matrix each player assumes for untagged 1280x720, are native and player behaviour not executed here.

A10 UNVERIFIED: port 49100 is hard-coded in both observe.py:78 and viewer/app.js:123, so --port changes HTTP only, and a second observer is outside the one-renderer-owns-the-pipeline limit. Native objects are created before the try (observe.py:65-78), but whether their destructors hang when server.start raises is native behaviour not executed; the session directory (exist_ok=False) is left behind either way.

A11 UNVERIFIED: observe.py:232 seeks via rt.seek -> update_from_usd_time, the retained-stage path. docs/recorded-pose-capture.md only says to use --snapshot-poses 'when' a recorded sequence does not advance; no repository record shows that failure for replay.usdc, and CLAUDE.md records update_from_usd_time driving sampled xform ops for the camera. The observer does not check that the image changes, but the failure itself is not established without a native run.

A13 REJECTED: a malformed run.json is skipped (observe.py:162) but is re-read every 0.25 s, so a transient non-atomic write recovers on the next poll and nothing wrong is stored. Only a persistently invalid file leaves the previous prompt/model fields, which is a writer fault, not an observer correctness failure.

A14 REJECTED: viewer_scene copies the authored start/end (265-266, 325-326) and physics_usd.export always authors both (57-58), so recorded replays, the documented input, get correct bounds. A hand-authored animation without a stage range is not a documented input, and static scenes legitimately have a zero range. Not a current-use contract violation.

A17 REJECTED as an independent defect: build_media copies fixed build paths by design and copyfile of a missing dolly.mp4 raises loudly (rerun fixes the mixed set). The proposed freshness/provenance system is what CLAUDE.md says not to add. The cheap, real part, the loop record covering only present.usda, is A15.
